strategy.summary: Konvertek (AT, group-owned, about 196 M EUR turnover, sound finances) is the sole active source for the 15 kW converter part:350021 under framework ctr:4600070540, which runs to mid-2027 with auto-renewal. It is a qualified but unused second source for the 7.5 kW part:350020, where it quotes well above the incumbent Selvbrunn. The price of 350021 has been flat since 2023 and sits about at our should-cost, so Konvertek earns roughly zero margin there. Cost drivers (electronic components, copper) have risen sharply. Konvertek has frozen its list for all customers until June 2027 and points to payment and logistics as the negotiable levers. We are a small account (about 0.6% of its turnover) to a supplier that is reviewing small accounts and facing a semiconductor shortage. Leverage is balanced, tilting toward Konvertek on 350021. On 350020, real competitive leverage exists through Selvbrunn. Strategy: protect supply and the flat price on 350021 by giving volume, length and payment, not by squeezing price. Use competition and should-cost only on 350020, and consider a bundle.
strategy.decision_maker: The key account manager negotiates within about 2%. Larger price changes go to a pricing committee that meets every two weeks (doc:20260711-70540-M3). The sales director sets account priorities (doc:20260223-70540-M2). A head-office directive bars discounts (quote:7300067, quote:7300003 remark).

A 24-month commitment gives a volume-focused supplier security and locks the flat price past the freeze. Longer adds nothing extra.

Only if it insists at renewal. Electronics and copper are at their peaks, so price the risk carefully and keep the base well below the fixed price.

price_view.reasoning: On 350021 the price sits at about our no-margin should-cost and drivers have risen substantially. The realistic aim is to hold the flat price, ideally extended for longer, not to cut it. On 350020 there is real room: Konvertek quotes far above both the incumbent and should-cost, though the should-cost models Selvbrunn's plant. A bundle could convert 350020 volume into a competitive 350020 price while keeping 350021 stable.

findings.text: Part 350021 (15 kW converter, Konvertek sole active source, quota 100%): price EUR 684.92 has been flat since 2023, and that price is 1.2% BELOW our own bottom-up should-cost of EUR 692.92 for its AT plant. The should-cost carries no margin and is said to be accurate to about 5%, so the gap lies within its error band. The fair reading is that Konvertek earns roughly zero margin on this part. There is no room to push the price down; the economic case points to holding it, not cutting it.

Cost drivers for 350021 have risen since the last price. Electronic components PPI rose 13.5% in 12 months (weight 0.43, about +5.8% on price). Copper rose 47.7% (weight 0.08, about +3.8%). Labour rose 2.7% (weight 0.15, about +0.4%). Together that is roughly +10% on the weighted cost base. All three indices are at their 36-month peak. Electronic components are only back to the 2022-10 high, not above it, and the price did not move down when the index was lower. Konvertek has nevertheless quoted the unchanged list price (684.92) and says its list holds for all customers until June 2027. Its history shows asks averaging +2.3% that settled at 0%. Any increase request in the 2027 renewal would be backed by real index data.

Part 350020 (7.5 kW converter, Konvertek qualified at 0% quota): Konvertek quoted EUR 466.99 on 2026-09-04. That is 15.8% above should-cost of EUR 403.21 and 13.1% above the incumbent Selvbrunn price of EUR 412.74. Caveat: this should-cost models Selvbrunn's DE plant, not Konvertek's, so it is a weaker benchmark for Konvertek. Konvertek's quote also rose 8.8% versus its 2025 quote of EUR 429.18. Index drivers support about +9.6%, so the rise is broadly index-consistent. Konvertek is consistently about 4-13% dearer than Selvbrunn on this part, with longer lead time (84 vs 49 days).

Cross-part economics are inconsistent. Konvertek prices 350020 well above cost, while 350021 sits about at cost. Bundling both parts could balance this: give Konvertek volume on 350020 at a price nearer EUR 413-430, while 350021 stays flat. Evidence on Konvertek's real cost structure is thin: the should-cost confidence is about 5% error and there is no Konvertek-plant estimate for 350020.

Not every market signal supports Konvertek's cost argument. Power prices are 43% below 2022. Copper and electronic-board inflation are real and published. Konvertek's own warning of a power-semiconductor shortage supports its pricing power.

findings.text: Pricing decisions sit with a pricing committee, not the key account manager: any change above 2 % needs committee approval, and the committee meets every two weeks. Expect the KAM to move freely only within about ±2 %. Larger moves add at least two-week cycles, so plan the timeline accordingly.

Red flag (frozen price list): Konvertek states its price list applies to all customers without exception until June 2027. It points to logistics and payment conditions as the negotiable levers. Unit-price cuts will meet a policy wall, so trades on payment days, Incoterm and volume are the likely currency. The 'without exception' line may also block increases until then; June 2027 matches the contract end date.

Red flag (deprioritising small accounts): the sales director said they are reviewing small accounts and will focus on customers with volume. We are about 0.6 % of its turnover, so Konvertek wants volume and binding commitments. Our rising forecasts are the counter (part 350020: 4580 vs 4154 units; part 350021: 1947 vs 1848 units).

Financially sound and stable: 196 M EUR turnover, 38.4 % equity ratio, credit index unchanged at 178, VDA 6.3 grade A, group owned. There is no financial stress to exploit, and Konvertek can afford to walk away.

Capacity constraint: in March 2026 Konvertek reported shortages of power semiconductors and extended lead times for frequency converters. It also has a fixed holiday shutdown (23 December to 6 January, with January call-offs due by 10 December). Availability is its lever; on-time delivery is weak at 81.5 %.

We are a fair payer: 2.1 days late on average and never more than 6 days late. However, 84.9 % of invoices are paid slightly late, which a sensitive supplier may raise. Paying on time or faster is a cheap gesture with real value to them.
Negotiation history on part 350021: across three renewals it asked for about +2.3 % on average and settled at 0 %. Its asks stay near the 2 % committee threshold, and it settles below its ask.

findings.text: Framework contract ctr:4600070540 covers only part:350021 (15 kW converter). It runs 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30 and extends automatically by 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice. To stop the renewal, notice must be given by 2027-04-01, so a credible exit window is still open.

Prices are fixed per calendar year. Any change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, i.e. by about 2026-10-02 for 2027. If Konvertek has not given notice by then, the contract supports holding the 2027 price at EUR 684.92. Its own e-mail of 2026-09-06 says its price list applies to all customers until June 2027.

Payment is 30 days net against our standard of 60, which is already a benefit to the supplier. Delivery is DAP with an 84-day lead time; planned lead time for the part is 56 days. The quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per supplier-caused complaint.

Price history on part:350021: three renewals asked +3.2%, +1.0% and +2.8% and all settled at 0%. The price has been flat at EUR 684.92 since 2023. Konvertek has repeatedly accepted a zero result. However, should-cost (EUR 692.92) suggests it already sells about 1.2% below cost, within the ±5% error.

Mutual dependency is asymmetric. Konvertek holds 100% of part:350021 (A-class, used in all pump series). Selvbrunn is qualified at 0%; its only quote was EUR 672 in Feb 2024 and is stale. Konvertek is a qualified 0% second source on part:350020, where an RFQ (rfq:6000000203) is open. Our roughly EUR 1.27 M spend is about 0.6% of its turnover. Its finances are sound and it has said it is reviewing small accounts.

Supply risk: Konvertek announced power-semiconductor shortages and longer lead times in March 2026. Its on-time delivery is 81.5% against the 95% contract target. Quality is 0 ppm. Its pricing committee approves price changes above 2%.

findings.text: Delivery is the weak spot: rolling 12 months to 2026-09 on-time is 81.5% against requested dates (85.2% against its own confirmations), well short of the 95% contractual target and below the peer median of 84.6%. It has also slipped from 88% in 2026Q1 and 84% a year earlier. When it is late, it is late by an average of 22.4 days (17.1 over all history), with a maximum of 41 days. All 27 receipts in the last 12 months are part:350021.

Quality is strong and argues its case. There have been 0 ppm and 0 complaints since 2026Q2, against a peer median of 457 ppm. Only two single-piece QNs have been raised since 2024, both on part:350021 and both recharged at the EUR 150 flat fee. Both 8Ds were closed in about 5 weeks and none are overdue. Defects cost us almost nothing.

The price of part:350021 has been flat at EUR 684.92 since 2023. Its three renewal asks (+2.3% on average) all settled at 0%. Our in-house should-cost of EUR 692.92 (±5%) suggests it sells slightly below cost, a point for the supplier if the part is strategic.

Volume outlook for part:350021 is stable to slightly rising: the 2026-09 forecast of 1947 pcs over the next 12 months compares with 1848 ordered in the last 12 months (+5.4%). The forecast is shared with the supplier, and snapshots have stayed in a steady 1800-2100 band. We are a small account to it, at about 0.6% of its turnover.

Ordering friction on part:350021 runs on both sides. On ours: 7 rush lines and 5 changed lines. On its side: 9 partial deliveries and 5 lines confirmed later than requested, the latest PO by 5 days. That PO's 2026-12-23 confirmation falls on the first day of the plant shutdown (23 Dec to 6 Jan). The data also has a known issue: requested and confirmed dates differ by 10-30 points, so OTD figures should be cited carefully.
Part:350020 is supplied by sup:70530, not this supplier. Its forecast data covers only sup:70530 and is relevant here only if we bundle or move it. Our order history shows sup:70530 at EUR 412.74.

arguments.text: Our 15 kW price has not moved since 2023 despite three requested increases (3.2 %, 1 %, 2.8 %), all settled at 0. We have absorbed the cost rise for the customer and have no room left.

Our cost drivers have risen sharply. Electronic components are +13.5 % in 12 months and make up about 43 % of the part. Copper is +47.7 % and at a 36-month peak. Assembled boards are +41 %. The 684.92 price sits at or below the customer's own no-margin should-cost of 692.92.
Our price list applies to all customers without exception until June 2027, and a head-office directive bars discounts. I cannot sell an exception internally.
Power semiconductors are short across the market. Allocation goes to customers who plan reliably and commit volume, not to those who press on price.
Quality is solid: 0 ppm over the last 12 months, scorecard class A at 90.7, and no overdue 8D reports.
The contract fixes the price per calendar year and runs to mid-2027. The customer has stable terms and should value that stability.

weak_points: On-time delivery is about 81.5 % against the contract target of 95 %, with late deliveries averaging 22 days and up to 41 days.
Our 7.5 kW quote of 466.99 is 13 % above Selvbrunn at 412.74 and up 8.8 % on our own 2025 quote. It is hard to justify.
Selvbrunn is qualified on the 15 kW part and quoted 672 in 2024, below our 702.43 at that time.
Industrial power prices are -43 % on 2022 and labour is only +2.7 %, so not all our costs are rising.
The customer pays almost on time (about 2 days late on average) and has never short-paid, so I cannot claim payment-behaviour pain.
Should-cost confidence is only 5 %, so my 'zero margin' claim is not proven either way.
Quantities and lead times are not firm: 7 rush lines on our orders, 84-day lead time versus a planned 56 days.
wants: A binding annual volume on the 15 kW part of about 1,950 pcs or more, with a longer commitment (24-36 months).
Volume on the 7.5 kW part (a share or bundle). For real volume I would sharpen the 7.5 kW price toward about 430.
Faster payment (for example 14 days) or strict on-time payment.
An index clause on electronic components and copper from mid-2027 as the alternative to a fixed increase.
Early, stable call-offs and an accepted 84-day lead time, with call-offs before the shutdown in December.
red_lines: No price cut on the 15 kW part. It sits at cost.
No fixed price beyond June 2027 without either an index clause or an increase.
No contractual 95 % on-time penalties during the chip shortage.
No higher complaint chargeback than the current EUR 150 flat fee.
Any change above 2 % only via the pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.
red_team.opening: I will thank the customer for a stable partnership with class A quality. I will point out that the 15 kW price has been held flat since 2023 despite electronics and copper inflation, and say the list is frozen for all customers until June 2027. I will then invite talks on payment terms, logistics, a binding volume and a longer commitment. In return I will offer to secure allocation of semiconductors and to discuss a bundled 7.5 kW share at a better price. I will signal that from mid-2027 an index clause or adjustment will be necessary.

rebuttals.answer: We recognise that the price has held for several years and we value that. It also reflects agreements both sides signed after open talks each year. Your own list commitment keeps it stable for now. Rather than argue the past, we would like to reward that stability going forward with a longer commitment, binding volume in line with our rising forecast, and better payment terms.

We do not dispute that electronics and copper have risen, and we take that seriously. Not every cost moved the same way, though. Energy is far below its earlier peak and labour has risen only moderately. Our should-cost estimate also has a wide error band, so it neither proves nor rules out a margin. We would rather address material risk jointly at renewal, for example with a fair clause or an agreed effective date, than through a fixed step now.
That same policy means the current price holds for all customers until next summer. Your note invites talks on payment and logistics, and that is exactly where we want to work with you.

We agree that reliable planning deserves priority, and we want to be that kind of customer. We share rolling forecasts and pay reliably. We are ready to commit binding volume and align call-offs with your shutdown and allocation planning. In return we expect on-time performance to move closer to the contract target.

Your quality performance is genuinely excellent and we say so openly. Quality and delivery belong together in the quality agreement, and delivery reliability is still below the agreed target, so the overall service picture is good but not yet complete.

We do value the stable framework. Extending it for a further term at today's conditions, with volume and payment improvements from our side, would give both sides the stability you describe beyond its current end.

press: We would welcome a plan with you to bring on-time delivery closer to the target in our quality agreement, since late receipts have recently averaged several weeks.
Part of your cost base, such as energy, has eased considerably, which we hope can be weighed alongside the material increases.
We have consistently paid reliably and in full, and we would like that to count when we discuss payment conditions together.
We are happy to give firmer call-offs earlier around your shutdown if that helps you confirm our requested dates more reliably.
